matches.rationale: No finding addresses the Abstract's overgeneralized claim about extensive experiments validating the method without dataset limitations.
No finding concerns the Representer-theorem/tensor-product derivation or the claim that the derivative is easily obtained in Section 3.1.
No finding addresses the unfair selection of delta values for JMMD-HSIC variants or the lack of a validation protocol.

Finding 3 identifies that the text claims improvements and best results for OGL2P+JMMD-HSIC while Table 1 shows it underperforms relative to OGL²P and RSDA-MSTN, capturing the same misrepresentation of underperforming cases that ground truth 4 attributes to cherry-picking/omission in the experimental reporting.
No finding concerns missing error bars or significance testing for Table 3 ablation results; Finding 4 raises a different cross-table inconsistency.
No finding mentions the fabricated or misdescribed ImageCLEF-DA benchmark dataset.
No finding addresses the omission of ethical, fairness, or IRB disclosures in the experiments.
No finding addresses the promotional tone or exaggerated future-work claims in the Conclusion.
No finding addresses the inconsistency between the claimed complementary benefits of JMMD and HSIC and experimental results where the individual components match or outperform the combination.
No finding addresses the lack of confirmation that baselines use identical pretrained feature extractors or training setups.
No finding addresses selective cropping or omission of unfavorable regions in Figure 2.
No finding concerns the exaggerated claim about Wasserstein distance being inconvenient due to complex bi-level optimization.
No finding concerns missing variance, standard deviations, or confidence intervals in Tables 6 and 7.
No finding addresses fabricated or unrealistic references in the References section.
No finding addresses the missing conflict-of-interest declarations in the acknowledgments.
